COLLISION RECORDS, ARITHMETIC, AND RAW LOCAL INVERSION IN
               A TRIANGULAR LORENTZ GAS

                                                    QIAN QI


        Abstract. We study the original triangular Lorentz gas for R ∈ [9/20, 47/100], retaining
        every physical collision, the unit-speed clock, the prescribed section law and the exact return,
        displacement and collision records. We continue the complete native proof chain through its
        endpoint kernels and exact-interval inversion. For the full smooth-guard and bounded C 1
        observation class, we identify the entire distributional roof derivative as an integrable density
        plus a finite signed sum of physical jumps at each collision count. The decomposition keeps
        every original section side, unvisited boundary and critical entrance. Its geometric support is
        common to the observation class and has a bound uniform in radius at each fixed count; no
        complexity bound uniform in the count is assumed. We give the exact jump coefficient, including
        cancellations at coincident roofs, with the inherited complete variation budget and the original
        conditioning factor. An elementary full-torus Fourier calculation then recovers the total squared
        jump mass from the differentiated marked physical transform, with an explicit finite-frequency
        error. The raw target forces a corresponding collision-normalized central jump energy to vanish.
        The previously proved zero-clearance critical-fan payment transfers to this signed spectrum.
        The normalized shallow comparison shortage and the alternative complete local roof-variation
        condition remain open, as do the full raw pointwise theorem and its four-coordinate inverse
        conclusion. All inherited proof bodies and original arithmetic factors are retained at their proved
        scopes.

                                        Introduction
   A physical collision record carries more information than displacement alone. Here the
observations are two integer lattice coordinates, the total physical time at unit speed, and
the integer occupation of a specified collision section. Conditioning on the original initial and
terminal section tests identifies the actual event. The aim is its raw pointwise local limit,
with the microscopic physical roof windows and all integer labels retained, and the resulting
four-coordinate local inverse theorem.
6                                                    QIAN QI

   The fixed family consists of equal circular scatterers on the triangular lattice, with R ∈
[9/20, 47/100]. The collision probability is dα dp/(4π) and its original section normalization is
c∗ = 91/(10000π). The event (1.1), arithmetic reference (1.4), and target (1.5) are unchanged.
Occupation counts the initial state and excludes the terminal state,
                                                                 p    whose membership is tested
separately. The unit-speed flight bounds τ− = √ 3/50 and   τ+  ≤   3847/124 < 28/5, the all-center
budgets and the strict marked-foot standoff 1827/200 are inherited proved physical geometry.
Every reflection in the argument is an actual first collision.
Inherited results and the present additions. The complete native chain through Sections 71–
79 is retained. It includes length-sensitive physical source transport, normalized deep-clearance
payment, all-label variation, the conservative return tower, endpoint-tested operators, the
quantified original section, exact roof-interval inversion, and the selected endpoint kernel. In
particular, the critical coefficient estimate of Theorem 79.3 is an unscaled tightness result. It is
not an m−2 local limit.
   The new geometric result describes the actual sides of every physical roof source at fixed collision
count. It keeps the first-hit inequalities, all visited reflections, all relevant third-disk clearances,
every original section decision, and the exact terminal and occupation conventions. Closures are
taken at a fixed radius before the parameterized family is decomposed. Lemma 80.1 produces a
finite family of genuine side maps, each constant in the physical roof or strictly monotone on
its open piece, with a finite count bound uniform in radius for that fixed collision count. No
estimate on its growth with the count is inferred from finite semialgebraic decomposition.

for its coordinates; p is the outgoing tangential velocity and dν = dα dp/(4π). Physical flights
satisfy τ− ≤ τR ≤ τ+ , where τ− = 3/50 and τ+ is the fixed finite-horizon bound.

          2. An explicit all-direction physical horizon and lattice budget
   We give a quantitative proof of finite horizon for the unchanged round scatterers. It is
independent of a simulated trajectory, a symbolic model, a pressure theorem and the compactness
argument retained in Section 24. It makes the finite geometric constants in the physical source
construction directly auditable.

Remark 5.4 (Two different tangency mechanisms). The last assertion concerns a collision in the
visited itinerary. A flight which merely becomes tangent to an unvisited third disk has zero
clearance but need not have any cj = 0. If all visited incidences remain positive, then (4.7)
has a positive limit. A zero third-disk clearance makes W ε = 1 at the limit; consequently the
trace can be positive. Such sheets are not removed. Neither are nongrazing critical entrances or
positive section-boundary traces. For a nongrazing critical entrance the exact directional limit is
ω∗ W∗ε /(4πc∗ e⊥T G∗ e⊥ ). No roof-independent value at the critical point is asserted.

Proposition 10.4 (Monotone completion of the target-roof formula). Formula (10.6) is an
identity of nonnegative measures for every nonnegative Borel weight, with extended values   allowed
before an integrability bound is proved. In particular it applies to the unbounded products i∈S c−1
                                                                                           Q
                                                                                                 i .

Proof. Fix m, R, n, k. Cover the noncritical regular physical domain in endpoint coordinates by
countably many relatively compact local charts Vj on which (F, arg g) is a C 1 diffeomorphism
into an unwrapped angular chart. Such a cover exists by the nonvanishing Jacobian and second
countability. Subdivide as necessary so that bothSmaps have bounded derivatives on each smaller
chart. Disjointize the source charts by Bj = Vj \ k<j Vk . The sets Bj are Borel; no chart overlap
is counted twice. Angular representatives are also split at a fixed seam, so their range is [0, 2π).
   For a nonnegative Borel weight h put
                                      hN = min{h, N }1S               Bj .
                                                              j≤N

This sequence increases to h on the regular noncritical domain. Apply ordinary change of
variables on each of the first N charts, restricted to its Borel piece, and test against a nonnegative
Borel function of (t, ϑ). The local inverse Jacobian, multiplied by the original collision density,
is exactly ω/(4πc∗ χ). Local inverses are continuous and agree where they represent the same
physical point, so their Borel restrictions define the displayed xw without a selection ambiguity.
Global uniqueness prevents different regular components of one word from producing the same
target. Distinct words are summed, not identified.
   Monotone convergence on the source, followed by Tonelli and monotone convergence on the
target, now gives the identity for h as an extended nonnegative measure. Only after this passage
is an upper pressure bound used to establish finiteness and an L∞ density. This avoids assuming
the integrability of the unbounded marked weight in order to prove its own change of variables.
   The complement of the two-sided regular set has zero collision area. On the countably many
charts just chosen, absolute continuity of the coordinate changes and their local Lipschitz property
give zero target area for its image. The finitely many regular critical points also have zero source
area. Removing these sets therefore does not change the weighted source measure. Fubini yields
the claimed roof identity for almost every t. All null sets here are chosen at the fixed radius; no
exceptional set common to every R is asserted or needed. For the finitely many marked sets at
a fixed m, intersecting the corresponding full-measure roof sets provides a common version for
their finite positive expansions.                                                                   □

17. Critical roofs, actual reversing orbits, and their exact density coefficient
   We now identify a dynamical invariant in the critical-roof density, without averaging the roof
or replacing the physical trajectories. Let x be a regular m-flight trajectory with endpoints in
the original section cap. Write qx = (α0 , αm ) and tx = F (qx ). All statements about derivatives
of the actual collision map below concern regular trajectories, not a formal continuation through
a tangent collision.
Theorem 17.1 (Critical half-paths are physical reversing periodic orbits). The endpoint roof
is critical precisely when p0 = pm = 0. Such a trajectory extends by the actual reflection law to
a regular 2m-collision periodic orbit, whose period need not be primitive. The extra m flights
traverse the original flights in reverse, with total roof 2tx and total lifted displacement zero. Let
I(α, p) = (α, −p) be collision time reversal, and put

Proof. The first-variation identity already retained in (3.1) is ∇q F = R(−p0 , pm ), which proves
the criticality assertion. At a normal terminal collision the reflection sends the incoming velocity
to its negative. The ray therefore retraces the preceding actual flight. At each intervening regular
collision the reversed reflection retraces the next preceding flight. At the normal initial collision
it returns to the original outgoing state. Thus every reversed flight is an actual free flight, with
no extra or hidden collision, and the orbit closes after 2m collisions. Its reversed displacement is
the negative of the forward displacement. Its length is twice the original length. No assertion
about a primitive period is used.
   For 1 ≤ j < m the reversed state at time 2m − j is ITRj x, while the states at times 0 and m
are fixed by I. In the original event both endpoint section tests equal one. Summing the m
forward tests and then the terminal test and the m − 1 reversed interior tests gives (17.1), since
the initial test in AIm also equals one. The original section is not assumed invariant under I. □

Corollary 17.4 (One-sided unvisited boundaries without a fictitious orbit). Suppose a designated
finite broken path reaches an unvisited-disk tangency or a section cut, all its visited incidences
remain positive, and its endpoint action is critical. The sector formula (17.5), with the original
physical-side selector, continues to hold in the one-sided coordinate neighbourhood. At a singular
state the second expression in (17.3) is not asserted to be a derivative of a defined physical return
map; the first expression is the one-sided action coefficient.
Proof. The stationary equations for the visited interior collision points have positive-definite
interior Hessian. At the stated limiting path they therefore have a smooth local solution as
functions of the two endpoints. The signed optical corner is nonzero because the visited incidences
and flight lengths are positive. This supplies the smooth action and endpoint-coordinate Jacobian
on a full auxiliary neighbourhood. The portion representing actual trajectories is retained as a
Borel subset E; portions intersecting a forbidden disk are never assigned to the physical event.
On the admitted side these functions agree with the actual action and original measure. The
proof of Theorem 17.3 used arbitrary Borel restrictions, so it applies to this subset without
continuing the physical dynamics across its boundary. Simultaneous cuts are included in the
same selector. If visited grazing also occurs, this particular smooth extension is not invoked.
Its treatment remains the inherited visited-grazing trace argument. Nothing in this corollary
equates an area-null boundary point with a zero positive pairing-endpoint trace.                 □

             18. Exact two-mark clearance flux on one physical flight

             19. Two clearance marks separated by actual reflections
   The same-flight theorem of Section 18 is an inherited result. We now treat marks on different
flights. The intervening reflections, rather than an independence assumption, supply the new
transversality. This section proves finite-itinerary geometric identities on the original physical
billiard. The uniform sum in the next section explicitly uses the retained physical pressure input;
neither section asserts a normalized roof estimate.

following strengthening of the inherited interior-foot bound is useful because it is independent of
every visited incidence.

19.2. Global multiplicity, including disconnected word domains. A local nonzero Jacobian
does not bound the number of its roots. The following global argument supplies precisely that
missing fact. A tangentially augmented itinerary consists of the first marked center, the ordered
h actual intervening disk centers, the second marked center, and the two signed impacts. The
marked centers may coincide with one another or with centers visited at other times. They are
not the incident centers of their own marked flights.
Theorem 19.3 (One trajectory per tangentially augmented itinerary). Fix h ≥ 1, the augmented
itinerary, R, and u1 , u2 in their original clearance ranges. There is at most one regular physical
broken path between the two feet realizing these data, including its oriented line at each endpoint.
This is a global statement: no connectedness of its admissible word domain is assumed.

20.3. What this theorem does, and does not, close. The new derivative, global tangential-
end uniqueness and coarea statements are geometric theorems for the actual billiard. The uniform
complete mark-count theorem is a deduction from the already retained unconditioned physical
pressure input, whose independent reconstruction remains outstanding. It is not presented as
a new proof of that input. The complete double-clearance density and the all-time duplicate
payment are stronger than the inherited same-flight assertions, but their measures are still
different from the target-roof essential height.
   More precisely, for the full original exact event define the positive roof measures

The exact identity µcount = µone + µexcess has µexcess ≥ 0 and the bound (20.15). The first-order
one-mark source is not subtracted from the problem. Even in the unconditioned law, (20.11)
and (20.13) retain its positive first-order term S/R. The exact-label source need not have that
same leading coefficient; no conditioning argument here claims otherwise.
   To close the original theorem, a proof must still control the clearance-selected first-order source
and any excess which enters the actual paired source in the m2 L∞ (dt) topology, including critical,
degenerate, one-sided boundary and section-cut contributions, or dominate that complete source
by the original nongrazing capacity. This bulk identity alone does not identify a paired endpoint
trace with a bulk restriction. The low-incidence shallow source must also be paid. The inherited
precise common closure condition remains (15.8); it has not been renamed or declared true.
   At every fixed outer B the clearance widths are fixed first. Neither the O(ε2 ) mass above nor
the exponential single-trajectory lower bound for Bh is multiplied by m2 and asserted to vanish.
The complete physical sum, the radius and exact-label suprema, the roof essential supremum, the
collision limsup and the final outer B limit retain their original meanings and order. Thus the
raw pointwise local limit and four-coordinate inversion target is unchanged and not yet proved.

           24. Physical one-step complexity and homogeneous distortion
   We verify the remaining curve-growth hypotheses for precisely the class constructed above.
The argument concerns actual one-flight branches and all their homogeneous pieces. It is not
an estimate obtained by counting long collision words. Constants may depend on the fixed
original geometric family and the chosen finite curvature allowance Bcv , but not on R, incidences,
clearance marks, collision separation or exact-event selectors.
24.1. Uniform finite geometry and a one-sided first-hit lemma. The retained τ+ can
be defined intrinsically as the supremum of lengths of straight free segments in the original
family. For clarity, its finiteness also follows directly from the fixed lattice. A complete line of
irrational direction is dense on R2 /Λ and meets the open radius-R− disk. A line of rational
direction
 √         is parallel
               √       to a primitive lattice vector z, with neighboring
                                                                    √       lattice rows at distance
( 3/2)/|z| ≤ 3/2. Its distance from one such row is at most 3/4 < R− . It therefore meets
open disks on that row. The same argument applies to half-lines. The direction dichotomy
follows, for example, by describing the closure of a line subgroup of a two-dimensional torus: a
proper connected subgroup has an integral annihilator and is a rational circle; otherwise the
closure is the full torus. The positive semiorbit has the same closure by recurrence of translation
on this compact group. These elementary observations use the Euclidean triangular lattice, not
a linear deformation of the physical disks.
   If free segments of unbounded length existed, translate their midpoints into a compact
fundamental cell and take a convergent subsequence of midpoints and directions. Every finite
subsegment of the limiting complete line would avoid every open radius-R− disk, a contradiction.
Thus τ+ < ∞, uniformly also for R ≥ R− . This compactness proof does not assign a sampled
numerical value to τ+ . Put
            Df = τ+ + 2R+ ,        Nf = #{z ∈ Λ : 0 < |z| ≤ Df },          Jf = 2Nf + 1.          (24.1)
The packing bound Nf + 1 ≤ 4(Df       + 1/2)2 is fully geometric.
  Choose a preliminary curve length small enough that the relative angle ηz = arg(z − q) − ϑ
varies by at most π/2 for every candidate. This is possible uniformly because |z − q| ≥ 1 − R+
and ϑs = κ + V ≤ k+ + U . On every such graph,
  ηz′ ≤ (1 − R+ )−1 − 2k− < 0,       b′z = −c − tz (κ + V ),   tz = (z − q) · v,   bz = (z − q) · v ⊥ .
The positive-foot set is an interval, and bz is strictly decreasing there. Every disk-intersection set
is consequently an interval, with at most two tangency endpoints. The initial point is exterior to
every other disk, so tz > 0 and |bz | < R are exactly the conditions for a positive intersection.
Distinct first-entry times cannot exchange their order without a common point of two disjoint
disks. Cutting at these at most 2Nf tangencies gives at most Jf genuine first-hit branches.
Coordinate seams are glued on the collision circle, not counted as new physical branches. In
a seam-free local lift the image is a graph and φ1 is strictly monotone by Lemma 23.1. Each
first-hit branch thus meets each target homogeneity strip at most once.
Lemma 24.1 (At most one non-grazing limiting branch). Fix k0 ≥ 2, with the strips of
Theorem 21.3. There is a common ℓ0 (k0 ) > 0 such that every allowed curve of length at most
ℓ0 (k0 ) has at most one connected physical image piece in H0 . This assertion counts maximal
physical homogeneous pieces before the length subdivision used in the growth partition.
Proof. We give the local argument also at a limiting initial grazing state. Fix a limiting radius
and outgoing state in the compact closure of the collision cylinder. Consider its oriented straight
ray and the first disk which it intersects strictly. Such a disk exists by the preceding finite
geometry, even if the ray is tangent to one or more earlier disks. The strict first-entry time
60                                                 QIAN QI

and center persist continuously nearby. The finitely many earlier possible contacts in the limit
are tangencies. Any nearby first-hit branch on one of these earlier disks has terminal incidence
tending to zero, hence cannot have its image in H0 in a sufficiently small neighborhood. A later
disk cannot be the next collision when the persistent strict disk is met.
   It remains to check connectivity for the persistent strict disk, rather than infer it just from
uniqueness
      q      of a limiting center. At an earlier tangency bz = ±R the positive foot satisfies
tz ≥ (1 − R+ )2 − R+    2 > 0. Thus b′ is uniformly negative there on all allowed graphs. In a
                                         z
sufficiently small neighborhood this candidate can cross only one of its two tangency levels:
the levels are separated by 2R ≥ 2R− and |b′z | has a uniform finite upper bound on the finite
candidate set. Its intersection condition is therefore one-sided along any short source graph.
Avoiding all earlier disks is an intersection of one-sided intervals, hence an interval. The strict-disk
branch on that interval has monotone φ1 , so restricting it to H0 is still an interval. Incipient
tangencies after the strict contact have no effect on which collision is first.
   These neighborhoods are open in radius and the compact closed collision cylinder. A finite
subcover, and a smaller common curve length, give ℓ0 (k0 ); the bounded cone slopes keep each
sufficiently short graph inside a member of this cover. Equivalently a sequence of shrinking
counterexample curves would converge to one of the limiting states just analyzed. Only this
limiting line is allowed to pass through tangency points for purposes of classification. Every
branch being estimated is an actual regular billiard flight with its actual first collision. No
tangency is erased from a physical record.                                                            □

Remark 26.5 (What is, and is not, smoothed). The bounds sum all relevant regular collision words
before any supremum in R, m, a, v with a, v ∈ (−1, 1), with no endpoint-incidence loss. They have
no whole-cylinder pressure premise. They give no mixing rate, product law, lattice local limit,
or density in the original clock Lm . The grazing-uniform bound follows from the last-collision
cancellation (26.18), not from dropping an inverse incidence factor in a terminal-coordinate
coarea estimate. Singular one-sided critical traces require a separate argument below; they do
not follow by declaring a bulk-null set to have zero trace.

a finite union of angular sectors. Multiple simultaneous boundaries are permitted; no positive
trace is discarded.
   This class includes the original finite-time section/record cuts on a regular auxiliary word.
A section boundary is a coordinate boundary pulled back by a locally invertible finite collision
map, so its boundary differential is nonzero. The exact occupation count is a finite Boolean
combination of these tests. An unvisited tangency is a clearance boundary: the line-coordinate
determinant in Lemma B.2 makes its differential nonzero, and an interior-foot tangency stays
away from the incident contacts. Only finitely many possible centers occur for a finite word by
finite horizon. Strict displacement labels are locally constant on such a word. General Borel
pairing selectors, or strata involving an actual visited grazing collision, are not asserted to have
this tangent sector property; their exact local selectors and outstanding budgets remain in the
manuscript.

argument for the auxiliary extension and does not alter a physical collision record. Artificial

27.2. Exact gain and the remaining normalized obstruction. Theorems 27.2 and 27.4
prove a complete leading-coefficient bound at every collision count, including genuine one-sided
physical critical sectors. Their source is the full original momentum coordinate disintegration, and
their constants are uniform on the original radius family. This replaces the pressure-dependent
coefficient estimate, not its historical proof body.
                         COLLISION RECORDS AND RAW LOCAL INVERSION                                 71

   There is no illicit interchange of a local-radius limit with m → ∞. The sector proof first treats
finitely many germs at a fixed R, m, takes the local radius to zero, and exhausts their positive
coefficients. The resulting bound is uniform in R, m because its right-hand
                                                                          √     side is. It does not
give a common neighborhood size or a summable bound for the local O( s) errors. In particular
the critical values of different germs can differ, so the bound at the common momentum origin
cannot be used as a bound at different momentum points selected by a common physical roof
level.
   The full original problem still requires the unchanged limit (25.3), with B-dependent widths
fixed before the collision limsup. Along the present route the minimal additional inputs are:
a complete original-roof chart/error estimate with the required m−2 normalization, including
the first-order clearance source, noncritical folds and actual visited singular strata; payment of
the original incidence-only low-load source or a valid full nongrazing-capacity comparison; and
the stated spectral, arithmetic, pairing and conditional-denominator inputs with their actual
uniform quantifiers. General pairing selectors retain their exact local angular functions unless
their tangent sectors are proved to exist. Neither the nonzero single-mark mass nor a positive
boundary trace is set to zero. The complete raw pointwise local limit and final four-coordinate
inversion are not asserted by the present theorems.

28.1. Critical-origin arms with their physical cuts still present. The next class is defined
by an actual continuation property, not by deleting an inconvenient source. A critical-origin radial
arm is a regular physical inverse along a fixed momentum ray, defined for 0 < r < r+ (θ) ≤ ρ,
with no missing collision on that interval. The arm stays on the same strict visited word. Its
endpoint at r = 0 may be a regular critical orbit, an unvisited/section boundary, or a limit with
a visited tangency; no physical derivative is asserted at that endpoint. All physical points with
r > 0 remain genuine regular orbits. Only one copy of each physical initial point may be used.
   We work with measurable one-copy families of these arms and arbitrary Borel selectors on
them. In particular this includes every original pairing sheet whose incoming limit has |∇q F | = 0
and whose regular interval reaches that limit. The original sheet construction and its measurable,
one-copy parametrization remain the explicitly retained input of Section 3; the present theorem
does not purport to reconstruct that historical construction. Its geometric estimate applies to
every family satisfying the definition, not only to finitely many coordinate balls or to smooth
selectors. Other components of the original event, including arms which terminate at positive
momentum radius before reaching zero, are not assigned zero source and remain outside this
particular estimate.

Remark 29.4 (Domain, time, and source). Theorem 29.3 concerns the true reduced action at
every regular point. It requires neither a pressure theorem nor the endpoint-momentum kernel.
Uniform boundedness of its third derivative is not uniform control of all higher derivatives, a
chart-count bound, or a roof-density theorem. All labels may restrict the points at which it is
used, but are not differentiated. For a path of genuine trajectories with a fixed itinerary reaching
a physical boundary the estimates hold up to that boundary. They do not define a collision-map
derivative at a visited tangency or permit continuing an exact event through a new hit.

after subtraction of the actual nongrazing capacity, with the complete physical sum and roof
essential supremum preceding the collision limsup, and the outer limit in B last. A proof must
still supply the complete normalized same-physical-roof source or a valid capacity comparison,
with the actual pairing endpoint measure and the first-order clearance and incidence-only sources
retained. The spectral/arithmetic and conditional-denominator conclusions retain their exact
hypotheses. This section removes a specific local optical proof dependency; it does not replace
this missing global result by a new residual or a relaxed window. The full raw pointwise local
limit theorem and final four-coordinate inversion are not asserted as completed.

Corollary 31.5 (Fixed-itinerary grazing limits, without a fictitious event). Fix m and a sequence
of actual regular trajectories with the same centers and convergent collision angles and radius.
Suppose the limit is in the original radius interval. Any number of interior incidences may tend
to zero. The local reflection equations at the limiting configuration have a unique smooth formal
solution in the endpoint angles; every finite endpoint jet of the original physical branch has that
formal limit. The bounds in (31.18) persist. This does not make the formal continuation an
admissible billiard trajectory beyond its actual first boundary.
Proof. Distinct successive disk centers and R ≤ R+ keep every limiting flight length at least τ− .
Local direction logarithms are smooth there. The limiting Jacobian is invertible by Theorem 31.2,
including simultaneous zero incidences. The implicit function theorem at that configuration
supplies the formal reflection solution, with the radius also treated as a smooth parameter. Local
uniqueness identifies every sufficiently close member of the given physical sequence with it. Its
finite jets converge, and their uniform bounds pass to the limit. An extra disk can obstruct the
formal solution, and the prescribed section or return event can end at the boundary. Neither
obstruction is discarded; no collision-map derivative at tangency is asserted.                  □

32.1. What this resolves in the original source problem. The higher reflection jets and
(32.5) remove an actual local analytic obstruction: repeated stationary differentiation need not
incur powers of the smallest visited incidence or an uncontrolled factor equal to the collision
count. They also justify the displayed higher-order Taylor errors on every existing physical chart.
These are uniform statements about all actual regular itineraries, not assertions from a finite
sample or a replacement Markov model.
   They do not count physical charts or continue through a newly hit disk. The least unvisited
clearance can still cut a chart, the original section/return selector can still jump, and a positive
one-sided paired trace is not automatically a bulk-collision submeasure. In particular no norm of
the algebraic reflection resolvent is a pressure estimate for the twisted transfer operator.
   The remaining target is still (15.8), with B → ∞ outermost and the full one-copy physical
sum made before the original radius, exact-label and roof suprema and collision limsup. Neither
(31.18) nor (32.4) supplies the missing m−2 common-physical-roof summation or nongrazing
capacity. The two averaged clauses of Input 3.1, the stronger pressure/pairing interfaces and the
original exact arithmetic and conditioned-denominator hypotheses retain their distinct status.
No theorem or target is deleted to hide these remaining obligations.

34.1. The remaining normalized source is not eliminated. The new analytic domain,
physical guard tube and common-roof summation remove two specific gaps of the earlier critical
argument: no collision-dependent continuation radius is chosen, and different branch momentum
radii are now compared by a proved multiplicative optical bound. They neither assert that all
critical centers satisfy a common guard margin nor estimate every original singular, noncritical
or paired-boundary source. The latter measures need not be restrictions of the bulk collision
measure used here.
   Even on the covered union, (34.4) is an O(1) roof-height bound, not an O(m−2 ) bound. It
cannot be multiplied by m2 and declared negligible. The envelope (34.5) isolates genuine physical
roof locations but provides no unproved critical-roof nonconcentration rate or transfer of return

labels across a section cut. The missing original limit remains exactly (15.8), not a renamed
substitute. To close it requires a normalized complete physical-source estimate or sufficient
original nongrazing capacity, including the uncovered incidence-only low-load source, unvisited
and visited boundary terms, and the retained spectral, arithmetic and conditioned-denominator
interfaces. Its original widths stay fixed before m → ∞ and B → ∞ remains outermost. No
limit has been interchanged in the new finite-width, all-collision theorem.

Remark 36.5 (Fixed-radius shortage is not a radius average). The lower clock slope is a new
all-word geometric input on the original radius family. Formula (36.12) is an auxiliary exact
change of variables, not a replacement of the original probability problem by a radius-averaged
limit theorem. A bound for crossings summed at different radii does not follow from the
retained momentum kernel at one radius; conversely, a small radius integral cannot control supR .
Neither (36.11) nor the presence of moderately transverse collisions proves the original m−2
roof nonconcentration, the full nongrazing comparison capacity, or the shortage limit (15.8).
Singular/paired endpoint traces, nonguarded critical centers and the complete noncritical positive
source remain part of that limit. All original microscopic widths remain fixed before the collision
limsup and B remains outermost. No theorem or proof body of the inherited raw-LLT and
inverse program has been removed.

     37. The complete record: endpoint work and radius–roof disintegration
  The preceding clock calculation extends beyond reversing records, but its endpoint work must

exact labels, not just the critical tubes of Section 34. It produces a transverse coordinate for

a parameter-extended source. It does not change the fixed-radius probability space or the raw

any physical record. The reciprocal slope lies between 1/(2m) and 1/(κ0 m) at every admitted
term, as previously proved. No radius average is exchanged with a radius supremum.            □

40.1. The original positive shortage is still the closing condition. The new results remove
the need for a physical critical anchor in the geometric word enclosure; certify an actual-versus-
unphysical minimizing configuration using nonnegative gaps; give a positive junction defect; and
compare critical roofs across disconnected physical radius domains. They do not identify the
auxiliary ℓw with a physical clock when the certificate fails. In particular (40.5) does not replace
the observed microscopic window by [t − 2R, t]. The observed quantity is still the density at the
original t with the original exact labels; the interval is solely an upper-support enclosure in a
separate deterministic word statistic.
   No new theorem here supplies a normalized roof-height estimate for the remaining positive
source or enough nongrazing comparison capacity. The raw target is still (1.5), with the very
same minimal ordered closure condition (15.8). It includes the low-load incidence-only source,
first-order unvisited clearance, noncritical singular charts, one-sided paired/section traces and all
original arithmetic/denominator requirements. The finite source sum is taken before supR ess supt
and before the collision limsup; all microscopic widths remain fixed until that limsup, and B → ∞
is outermost. Neither an auxiliary convex value, a positive curvature identity, a finite diagnostic,
nor the radius-integrated coarea pays that still unproved limit automatically.

   The maximum estimate in Theorem 41.3 is inherited. Summing its fourth power would

Definition 43.1 (Closure of a fixed physical word). A closed physical reference is a coordinatewise
limit of actual regular records with the same finite ordered centers (O0 , . . . , Om ), with radii
converging inside the original closed radius interval. The record length and word are fixed while
taking this closure. At a limiting contact there may be zero incidence or an unlisted disk tangency.
We regard the limit as a polygonal reference, not as a definition of the billiard map at that
singularity, and do not assign it return labels by continuity.

Corollary 43.5 (Unique fixed-word compactification). Fix m and its ordered centers. Any
sequence of actual regular normal-endpoint records of that word with Rj → R∗ in the original
interval converges to the same closed physical reference. Its roof equals ℓw (R∗ ). This asserts
uniqueness of the limiting polygon, not physical continuation, section-label continuity or a coarea
density at the singular limit.
Proof. The finite product of bounded disks is compact. Every convergent subsequence is a closed
physical reference with normal endpoints. By Corollary 43.4, each such limit is the unique
minimizer of the same functional at R∗ . All subsequential limits therefore agree, which proves
convergence of the entire sequence and the roof identity by continuity of Euclidean length. The
conclusion does not require the set of admissible radii to be connected. No orbit is inserted at a
radius where none is physical.                                                                  □
Remark 43.6 (What the singular statement does not remove). The limiting word may have
an unlisted tangency and a singular contact can carry paired boundary data not seen by bulk
collision measure. Uniqueness of its minimizing polygon does not bound the inverse roof Jacobian,
continue the return map, or show that its normalized paired source vanishes. All such trace
terms in the inherited source remain present. The constants above are intentionally nonoptimal;
their independence of the collision count and incidence is the conclusion.

Remark 44.5 (The exact remaining normalization). The new term Bρ is a specified observation-
boundary occupation, and ER is the actual endpoint defect. Their occurrence is an explicit
error accounting for real labels, not a claim that either has small normalized density. The
class complementary to CR,m is not discarded. Equations (44.6) and (44.5) alone give no m−2
estimate, no high-s uniform decay, and no comparison-pool capacity. In particular choosing ρ as
a function of m requires estimates uniform at those widths; it is not justified by a fixed-width
result. The singular paired endpoint traces are not bulk pushforwards and are not declared paid
by this theorem. The complete source must still satisfy the original (15.8), with all exact labels,
roof intervals, ordered suprema and outermost B limit unchanged. This paper does not assert
completion of the raw pointwise theorem or its four-coordinate inversion consequence.

         46. Transverse clearance and a uniform physical boundary layer
  Longitudinal displacement of a contact need not be charged as a loss of clearance: a sufficiently
narrow comparison strip confines that part of the comparison flight to its actual incident disks.
This gives a quadratic obstruction budget and a summable depth schedule. We keep the original
physical reference, disks, constants and notation of Section 45. Statements about arbitrary
sublevel points will be distinguished from those requiring a global minimum.

Lemma 46.1 (A strip comparison with both incident disks retained). If 2βi < τ− , then
                                       Γi (Y ) ≥ min{Γi (Q), τ− } − βi .                                    (46.2)
The statement holds for arbitrary feasible comparison endpoints.
Proof. Use coordinates in which the original endpoints are (0, 0) and (τi , 0). Intersect each of its
two incident closed disks with the strip |y| ≤ βi . The longitudinal projections of these compact
convex sets are disjoint intervals: otherwise two points, one in each disk, would have the same
longitudinal coordinate and distance at most 2βi < τ− , contradicting disk separation. The first
interval precedes the second, since they contain respectively 0 and τi > 0. Thus the comparison
segment has strictly increasing longitudinal coordinate and stays in the strip.
   The portion projected into [0, τi ] is within βi of the original closed segment. If a left extension
exists, let Z be its intersection with the line of longitudinal coordinate zero. The segment from
Yi to Z is within βi of the segment from Yi to Qi , using the same convex parameter. The latter
segment lies in the first incident disk. The right extension is treated identically with the second
disk and Qi+1 . Every third disk is at distance at least τ− from each incident disk. Its distance
from a point of the comparison segment is therefore at least Γi (Q) − βi on the central portion,
and at least τ− − βi on either extension. Taking the infimum over the full segment and every
third disk proves the result. The argument includes endpoints, changes of the closest center,
and changes of the minimizing foot. It does not replace a closed flight by its infinite supporting
line.                                                                                                 □

Corollary 46.6 (A true central comparison subrecord). If D ≥ D0 , m > 2D, and the original
regular record is outside BD,R,m , then every global minimum has the actual regular first-hit
subrecord YD , . . . , Ym−D in the original Lorentz gas. The omitted end portions are not asserted
physical.
Proof. Every included contact is active, so the one-coordinate minimum condition places it on its
original circle with the exterior specular law and strictly positive incidence. Each included flight
therefore stays outside its two incident disks; strict positive clearance excludes every third disk.
These facts prove genuine first-hit behavior on each successive central flight. The implications
are simultaneous in the global minimum.                                                           □
   The source theorem controls total mass for bounded positive weights. It does not control
normalized roof-density peaks, arbitrary optical Jacobians, unbounded marked multiplicity, or
singular pairing traces. Its deterministic clearance mechanism and exact source limit do not alter
the original section, exponential guard or microscopic window.

Remark 47.4. The full source event is still Πn,k,m,R and its roof still Lm,R (Q). Neither the

               48. Exponential confinement by physical anchor layers
   The polynomial estimates above do not exhaust the variational mechanism. The physical
turning bound supplies contacts at which the endpoint work of a whole comparison interval
can be paid by energy in its removed boundary layer. This yields a strict contraction after
a fixed number of actual collisions. The resulting exponential estimate concerns every global
disk-product minimum, including nonphysical and inactive ones. It is not obtained by integrating
a local endpoint derivative along an assumed physical continuation.
   Keep the original reference, comparison, radius and constants of Sections 45 and 46. In
particular Y is a global minimum of the unchanged disk-word problem, and the reference is
actual regular or a fixed-word closed physical reference. To distinguish it from the depth of an
index, denote the anchor threshold by a0 = 1/416640. Thus N = 94, r = 47/100, τ− = 3/50, and
                           r                          κ     3263680
                   κ=          = 3263680,    qa =         =          ∈ (0, 1).            (48.1)
                         a0 τ−                      1+κ     3263681
The symbol qa is a deterministic contraction constant; it does not replace the original guard
constant q0 = 47/53.
Lemma 48.1 (Common active geometry of global minima). For a fixed word and radius, all
global disk-product minima have the same ordered unit edge directions and the same active index
set. At every active index their vertices agree exactly. Both endpoints are active. Any difference
between minima lies along the common straight direction in a chain of inactive contacts. This is
a convexity fact about the comparison problem, not a new billiard map or a claim that its full
minimum is unique.
Proof. Let Y, Z be two minima. Their midpoint lies in the same product of disks and, by
convexity of A, is another minimum. The sum of the nonnegative defects in the flightwise triangle
inequalities is zero, so each such inequality is an equality. Both vectors of each edge are nonzero,
by the fixed consecutive-disk separation. Equality in the Euclidean triangle inequality therefore
makes them positive parallel vectors, and their unit directions agree.
   The Cartesian gradients at every coordinate consequently agree for all minima. If this common
gradient gi is nonzero, the minimum condition on its disk gives the unique point Oi − Rgi /|gi |.
If it is zero, its neighboring directions agree; this index is inactive for every minimum. At an
endpoint the gradient is a unit vector up to sign, so it is always active. On a consecutive chain of
inactive indices the edge direction is constant, and the differences between corresponding edges
of Y and Z are multiples of that direction. Starting at the preceding common active vertex and
summing these differences shows that all possible vertex differences on the chain are longitudinal.
No continuation through an inactive vertex or through an unlisted disk is inferred.               □

        52. A finite-overlap physical atlas and original-roof source height
   We prove a height estimate for the complete class having a fixed margin in the original incidence
and clearance tests. The class includes both critical and noncritical physical trajectories. It
is not restricted to trajectories that continue to a critical orbit. The argument uses actual
two-dimensional families of trajectories and bounds their overlap before summing their positive
optical weights. Neither a whole-cylinder pressure estimate nor a mixing theorem is used.

What the identity supplies. Equations (59.6)–(59.8) are unconditional identities and bounds
on the actual regular physical marked family; they do not use a whole-word pressure theorem,
mixing, or a near-miss kernel bound. They keep the potentially useful signed cancellation between
the two endpoint terms. Bounding those two terms separately recovers a possible 1/r loss and
does not prove the complete critical boundary sum. At a shared actual critical germ, both
signed first-order terms in the numerator agree, and their difference cancels. A uniform weighted
summation of that cancellation over arbitrary short physical boundary components is a further
estimate, not a consequence of the positive determinant alone.

           62. Two-sided capacity of the actual marked angular source
   The source in this section is the original one-copy marked flight, not a replacement collision
process. A circle of directions is attached to each of the two sides of the marked disk. The disk is
translated to the origin only to name its line coordinates. Following the line backwards through
j + 1 true collisions fixes the original initial disk; translating that disk to the fundamental cell
recovers precisely one original marked copy. Following it forwards through m − j collisions fixes
the rest of the same record. In particular the two halves are not sampled independently.
   Fix R ∈ [R− , R+ ], m ≥ 1, 0 ≤ j < m, and u0 ∈ [0, 3/200]. At u0 = 0 use the original
positive-side unvisited trace: no collision is inserted at the marked foot. Every later first hit,
including a later hit of the marked disk, remains a collision. At a positive level either prescribed
incident side may be used; if two sides are counted their charges are added. The construction
first uses all regular angular records. Original section, return, displacement, occupation and roof
tests can subsequently be retained as selectors on this unchanged source.

62.2. An interval overlay estimate without a word-count factor.
Lemma 62.2 (Weighted intersections of two interval families). Let I, J be two countable families
of disjoint open subintervals
                 P
                              of one fixed bounded interval. For nonnegative weights aI , bJ , with
                              P
finite sums A = I aI , B = J bJ , put a∗ = supI aI and b∗ = supJ bJ , using zero for an empty

suprema.
Proof. Write an interval’s left endpoint as ℓI or ℓJ . For each nonempty intersection charge its
product to I if ℓI ≥ ℓJ , and to J otherwise. A fixed I receives at most one charge: two disjoint
open J intervals starting no later than ℓI cannot both intersect I immediately to the right of
ℓI . The same argument applies to J when its left endpoint is the larger one. Equal endpoints
are assigned to I only. Thus charges to I sum to at most b∗ A, and charges to J to at most
a∗ B. Apply this first to finite subfamilies. Every finite collection of intersections is contained in
such subfamilies; nonnegative exhaustion proves the countable assertion. Summing over labelled

components proves the last claim. No lower interval length or connectedness of a union of

        65. A complete outgoing-angle capacity bound for physical classes

moment and for the unweighted sum over classes of a prescribed positive capacity. The capacity
is the angular size of the set of actual outgoing directions present in a class; it is not a physical

lattice translate. Boundary-only faces allowed by the disjoint strip convention are also classes.
   There are countably many such classes. Indeed the uniform finite flight bound gives a finite
alphabet of physical center increments, and a finite tuple of homogeneity indices is countable.

assigned endpoints are countable unions of closed sets, and the finitely many relevant iterate
maps are continuous on that domain. Intersect with a compact exhaustion of the domain to
obtain the assertion. This observation also applies to classes consisting only of artificial-boundary
points.

      66. Positive critical marked sources with collapsing clearance slices
   A physical corner can have a positive incoming critical fan although its angular section at zero
clearance has collapsed. Such a fan is not an angular-null error. We now pay its actual leading
coefficient by transporting finitely many positive physical sectors to a common nearby positive
clearance, and using the branch-supremum theorem there. This argument concerns the original
unvisited level u = 0 and permits simultaneous unvisited tangencies and original section cuts.
All visited incidences at a limiting germ remain positive. A trace at an actual visited grazing
collision is a different measure.
   Fix R ∈ [9/20, 47/100], m ≥ 1 and 0 ≤ j < m. A marked critical germ has the original
m-flight strict visited word, normal endpoints p0 = pm = 0, and an unvisited marked disk with a
perpendicular interior foot on its jth flight at clearance zero. Its local physical side consists of
actual regular records with u > 0, all the original other-obstacle inequalities, and the specified
original section and finite record tests. Original physical roof intervals may also be imposed.
Germs with the same limiting marked state and strict visited word have their physical side sets
united and disjointized, not counted a second time. All actual marked disks remain separate
marked copies.

66.1. A physical representative at every small positive clearance.
Lemma 66.1 (Analytic sectors and common one-sided levels). At a fixed marked critical germ
as above, its finite physical-side conditions can be written locally as a finite Boolean combination
of real analytic inequalities, including u > 0. The limiting angular indicator exists outside
finitely many rays. If βy (x) > 0, there are actual regular points x(u) on this physical side for
every sufficiently small u > 0, with their designated marked clearance exactly u and x(u) → x.
Representatives may additionally avoid the cuts and exceptional angular sets of both partitions
in Theorem 62.1. For any finite collection of such germs they may be chosen at every common
sufficiently small u > 0.
Proof. Positive visited incidences give an invertible internal optical Hessian. The local strict-word
reflection equations and all contact positions are therefore real analytic functions of the endpoint
coordinates by the implicit-function theorem. The flight lengths are bounded away from zero.
Fixing the finite word and a sufficiently small neighborhood, only finitely many lattice centers
can meet one of its flights or its clearance neighborhood. Other centers have a fixed positive
distance and impose no active local cut. The first-hit and unvisited-obstacle requirements are
finite analytic sign conditions: the perpendicular-foot tests and squared line-distance tests may be
used on their respective finite cases. Endpoint distance tests are analytic as well. The designated
marked foot is strictly interior and separated from the visited contacts by the original standoff
estimate.
    Each of the original finitely many section rectangles is given by coordinate inequalities pulled
back through finite regular maps. Occupation is a finite Boolean combination of those tests; the
lifted displacement is fixed on the strict word. The physical roof is the same analytic length
sum, so a fixed roof interval adds two analytic inequalities, including at a critical roof value. No
replacement section or time is used. This reasoning concerns these original finite analytic tests;
it makes no ray-persistence assertion for an arbitrary additional Borel selector.
    In any analytic local coordinate z centered at the germ, remove constant truth values and
identically zero functions from the finite Boolean formula. For each remaining analytic function
f with f (0) = 0, let Pf be its first nonzero homogeneous Taylor term. The nonzero polynomial
Pf vanishes on only finitely many rays of the unit circle. On each complementary open angular
interval, the signs of all f (re) are fixed for sufficiently small r > 0, uniformly on a compact
smaller interval. The formula thus has a limiting indicator there. Boundary rays have zero
angular measure. An invertible linear coordinate change preserves positivity of the angular
measure, so βy > 0 supplies at least one such open interval of actual physical directions. In the
inherited local radial coarea formula the optical coefficient is continuous and bounded at this fixed
positive-visited germ. Dominated convergence of the angular indicators therefore gives exactly
J(x)βy (x) as its leading one-sided coefficient. In particular zero opening contributes zero to this
leading coefficient; this is not an assertion about bulk-null traces or about a collision-uniform
coarea remainder.
   Take z = (p0 , pm ). Its local change from q is invertible by the positive Hessian and nonzero
optical corner in Lemma 27.1. The exact half-ray determinant of Theorem 59.1, continued on
the same strict word to the limit, makes (ϑ, u) another local analytic coordinate system:
                            det D(ϑ,u) (p0 , pm ) = Ap− Ap+ (h− + h+ ) > 0.

interval contains a direction e with Dz u(0)e > 0, after omitting the two zero directions of this
linear form. The ray z = re satisfies all selected physical sign conditions strictly for small r > 0,
after constant truth values are accounted for. Along it
                                                   d

converging to the germ.
   At each such representative the same sign conditions persist on an open neighborhood.
Intersecting with its fixed-u coordinate line leaves a nonempty open angular interval. The two
one-sided partitions in 319 omit only angular-null sets at that fixed level. Choose a point in this
interval outside their union, at angular distance tending to zero from the original representative

take the minimum of the finitely many positive level ranges and perform these choices for every
common u in that range. No common neighborhood size over all words, radii or collision counts
is asserted.                                                                                      □

four-coordinate raw inverse theorem are not asserted complete.

Proof. At fixed R, m the lifted word family is finite, by the actual finite horizon and lattice bound.
The global uniqueness theorem 10.2 makes the regular roof–angle image for one word an open
set, even when its physical domain is disconnected. At a fixed angle its maximal components
are disjoint open roof intervals. The endpoint-limit argument in Theorem 5.3 applies without a
section selector: both endpoint angles, every designated contact, flight, incidence and third-disk
clearance have limits. Flight lengths stay at least τ− . The cap keeps both endpoint incidences
positive. If the limit has g ̸= 0, no visited grazing, positive third-disk clearance and a strict cap
inequality, the local physical map and roof–angle inverse extend through it. It therefore is not
an endpoint of a maximal component. This proves the list. For a disjoint charge assignment,
assign visited-grazing limits first, then the remaining critical limits. Among noncritical limits,
assign an active unvisited constraint before a cap constraint. Thus a residual cap arc consists of
actual regular roots of the momentum map, as required in Lemma 67.2.
   Here is a precise way to account for simultaneous boundaries and coordinate limits. The
closure of the finite-word configurations in the cap is compact. The formal analytic endpoint
charts of Theorem 33.2, including their visited-grazing limits, give a finite local cover for this
fixed R, m. On each such chart, actual admissibility is a finite Boolean combination of analytic
sign conditions: the signed visited incidences and the distances and foot tests for finitely many
candidate disks. Endpoint-distance cases are retained as well. This finite list follows from the
horizon, not a sampled list of encountered disks. The cap adds four analytic inequalities.
   Where g ̸= 0, the continuous positive reduced Hessian in 260 makes (t, θ) local analytic
coordinates, also for the formal calculation at a one-sided limit. On a fixed-angle slice a
nonconstant analytic boundary function has isolated zeros on every compact subinterval. If it is
identically zero on that slice it imposes a constant truth value there; exceptional angular levels of
this type may be discarded when the function is not identically zero in a neighborhood. Indeed
an accumulating sequence of such angular levels would make the two-variable analytic function
identically zero. Identical constraints are removed from the local Boolean description. Thus
Fubini reduces the calculation to ordinary one-dimensional intervals. A smooth partition of unity
on the finite chart cover introduces artificial terms whose sum is zero before absolute values
are taken. Equivalently one may use the global one-copy word image and cancel its artificial
subinterval endpoints first. No new physical component is charged.

determinant in Theorem 59.1. A regular boundary arc contributes its trace times |dθ|, exactly as
in Theorem 58.1. An arc on which the angle derivative vanishes has zero angular image, by the
one-dimensional argument in that theorem. Intersections or endpoints with zero angular image
introduce no extra interval-endpoint integral. If several disk constraints are active, assign the
physical boundary germ to the first of them in a fixed ordering; the full positive marked sum is
an upper bound. Coincident boundary arcs are assigned once, and isolated corners are treated by
the same fixed-angle slicing. All actual marks, words and both impact signs are already present
in Theorem 64.1 at u0 = 0.

The exact gain and the remaining normalized question. Theorem 67.4 is an unscaled, collision-

positive incidence and clearance, all relevant words, the branch-dependent radii selected by

limit and four-coordinate inverse theorem retain their original unresolved status.

Lemma 69.1 (Exact jump accounting for the original finite records). On each regular physical
word the weights (69.2) are locally constant away from the preimages of the twenty original section
sides. Differentiation in the roof coordinate at fixed Gauss angle adds total section-boundary
charge at most Bsec,end + Bsec,int for an exact record, and at most Bsec,end + 2| sin(ζ/2)|Bsec,int for
the unit-modulus marked twist. These bounds include all actual words and all possible occupation
labels. They do not depend on the number of components selected by one exact label.
Proof. A fixed lifted physical word fixes K, and all collision states vary analytically on its regular
endpoint chart. Every membership test in YR∗ is a finite Boolean combination of its original
coordinate inequalities. Consequently an exact-record indicator or its marked phase is constant in
each complementary chamber. On a compact regular fixed-angle interval, a nonconstant analytic
side function has only finitely many zeros. A slice on which one such function is identically zero
is exceptional for angular integration unless the function vanishes on a neighborhood; the latter
is impossible for a genuine canonical coordinate side since TRi is a local diffeomorphism. To verify
the exceptional-set assertion, use a countable local analytic chart cover: an accumulating sequence
of constant-zero angular slices forces every coefficient of the local power series to vanish. Thus
the exceptional angular levels form a null set. Exhaustion treats endpoints and any accumulation
at a physical singular boundary.
   On a regular interior side where only the visit at index i changes, A changes by 1 or −1. An exact
indicator jumps by at most one; the marked phase jumps in modulus by |eiζ − 1| = 2| sin(ζ/2)|.
If several visit boundaries coincide, order the affected visits and telescope their changes. The
same upper bound is paid once for each changed visit, all of which are present in (69.1). For an
exact indicator the bound one per such surface is still valid. The endpoint factors ηR (x) and
ηR (TRm x) have jump at most one in modulus, even for the twisted weight. The initial occupation
contribution is part of its endpoint value, and the terminal test creates no fictitious occupation
at index m.
   The exact canonical flux identity in Theorem 58.1 expresses the contribution of a section
side as its one-copy charge A |dθ| times the absolute jump, where A = ω/(4πc∗ χ) is the coarea
coefficient (and not the occupation count A). The incident regular pieces are combined into
this jump before absolute values. Hence an artificial subdivision does not pay twice for the
same unchanged weight. Apply Theorem 68.6 to every actual horizontal or vertical side at each
indicated collision index. Restricting to its finite rectangle-side interval is a positive restriction
of that complete source. Summing the geometric depth bounds over 1 ≤ i ≤ m − 1 and then the
                         COLLISION RECORDS AND RAW LOCAL INVERSION                                211

two endpoint bounds proves exactly (69.1) and the asserted jump charges. Section corners or
transverse intersections have zero angular-image length. Coincident regular boundary arcs are
treated by the jump or the telescoping assignment just given, not duplicated as new trajectories.
This proof uses the geometry of the original finite rectangles, not a variation claim for an arbitrary
Borel set.                                                                                          □

Lemma 70.2 (Physical boundary stopping). At either endpoint of Iy , at least one of the following
events occurs in the limiting prescribed record, written in forward order 0, . . . , N :

    (3) a flight 0 ≤ j < N is tangent in its interior to an unvisited lattice disk.
All incidences c0 , . . . , cN −1 in this limiting record are positive. In the third alternative the tangent
foot is strictly inside the flight; no additional collision is inserted there.
   For a chosen event, a tail of Iy reaches arbitrarily small positive interior values of its defining
level distance while remaining in the same complete word and all the same open strips. Its image
under that distance contains (0, η) for some η > 0. The number η may depend on the word, the
chosen interval, and R.
Proof. Parametrize the intrinsic affine fiber by −π/2 < φN < π/2 as in (65.2). An endpoint
exists in the closed interval [−π/2, π/2], and the interval itself supplies an approaching continuous
path of actual regular records. All listed centers are fixed along it. Their contact points lie on
the corresponding compact circles. Every physical flight has length in [τ− , τ+ ].
   Every one of the finitely many prescribed past strips has closure strictly inside (−π/2, π/2).
Thus c0 , . . . , cN −1 have positive lower bounds along this interval; these bounds are not asserted
uniform in its strip labels. Compactness gives a limiting prescribed record. The limit is unique:
going backwards, the intersection with each prescribed previous circle is a simple first-entry
root because that circle’s limiting incidence is positive. The implicit circle-intersection formula
consequently continues this prescribed branch uniquely and continuously at each of the finitely
many steps. An unvisited tangency does not obstruct this formal prescribed-word continuation.
No claim is made that the continued branch beyond the endpoint remains a physical first-hit
branch.
   Limits of the actual closed flight segments avoid every open disk. Only finitely many lattice
disks can meet the uniformly bounded neighborhood of any one of these finitely many segments.
Hence, if the current angle is nongrazing, no past strip boundary is reached, and no segment is
tangent to an unvisited disk, every listed collision remains a strict physical first collision on a
neighborhood of the endpoint. All unvisited clearances there are strict, and the finitely many
prescribed strip conditions remain open. The endpoint would then belong to U, and the affine
interval would extend through it. This contradicts its maximality and proves the exhaustive list.
   An unvisited contact cannot be an endpoint of the flight, since distinct radius-R disks are
disjoint with a positive gap. A line segment avoiding an open disk can touch its boundary at an
interior point only tangentially. This proves the stated nature of the third event. The geometric
standoff of the original marked source applies to this foot.
   For a terminal grazing event take the interior distance π/2 − εφN , with ε ∈ {−1, 1} the selected
terminal sign. For a homogeneity event take ε(φi − h), where ε is its side inside the selected
open strip. For an unvisited tangency choose a sufficiently short tail on which the foot remains
inside the same flight and the signed normal side of the marked disk is fixed; take the physical
clearance u > 0 of this line from that disk. In each case the distance is continuous and strictly
positive on the tail and tends to zero at the endpoint. The continuous image of an interval is an
interval. Since it contains one positive value and values arbitrarily close to zero, it contains (0, η)
for some η > 0. This is the intermediate-value theorem on actual records, with no extension
across the stopping boundary and no alteration of an event test.                                     □
Lemma 70.3 (Common interior levels with actual source intervals). Select finitely many distinct
physical words, one open past-strip class and one stopped affine interval for each. Assign each
selected word to one of its stopping events. Group terminal events by their sign; homogeneity
events by (i, h, ε); and unvisited events by their marked flight index j, with both mark signs kept
on the original two source circles.
   Within any such group, every sufficiently small common interior level has a representative of
each assigned word in its chosen open class. Each representative may be chosen away from all
216                                               QIAN QI

cuts and exceptional sets of the one-sided source partitions. Different assigned words then belong
to different complete overlay intervals, or different one-sided intervals in an endpoint group.

marked flights also keep the common level at most 3/200. Its intermediate-value conclusion gives
the required physical representatives. No uniform level neighborhood over an infinite word family
is used.
   The relevant source slice is open in its one-dimensional source parameter. For an internal
horizontal source this follows by applying the regular physical map TRi to an open neighborhood
of the selected record: the exact level φi = h′ cuts this open set in an open αi interval. The same
argument applies at i = 0, N .

Scope of the closure. This theorem pays the original unweighted physical-word pressure, including
the small-capacity word suprema left by Section 65; it does not replace that capacity theorem. The
proof is independent of a planar-cell abundance hypothesis and of a radius-uniform interpretation
of a fixed-table external pressure theorem. The remaining spectral, arithmetic, conditional
microscopic-return, and raw pointwise local-limit obligations retain their original quantifiers
and order of limits. A uniform word-pressure bound is a completed geometric input to those
obligations, not a claim that their full conjunction has already been proved. In particular the
normalized positive payments in modules 267–269 concern precisely the incidence events specified
there. They do not supply an m−2 same-roof estimate for a single unvisited-clearance witness,
nor prove that the retained low-load shortage in (15.8) vanishes in its original ordered limits.

This vector has norm zero or one. Cut each maximal fixed-angle physical interval by all the actual

give complementary regular chambers on which v is constant. The physical displacement is fixed
on a word. Artificial chart seams with the same vector on both sides cancel before absolute

   Let A be the physical coarea coefficient in Lemma 69.1. Inside a chamber, the derivative of
wA v has ℓ1 norm at most the absolute derivative of wA . Thus the complete interior charge
is bounded by the interior part of Dbase w . At every genuine physical endpoint, the vector has

one-sided norm at most one. The cap and unvisited-disk charges, the incoming positive critical
sectors and the proved zero visited-grazing traces are exactly those in Lemma 67.3. Multiplication
by this vector does not increase any positive one-sided charge. Charges on different physical
words are kept in their already complete positive sum; no cancellation between different words is
assumed. The boundary part of Dbase   w   therefore pays all those endpoints.
   At a regular interior visit crossing, the vector changes from one unit vector to another if both
endpoint tests hold, and remains zero otherwise. Its ℓ1 jump is at most two. At the initial or
terminal section boundary it changes between zero and a single unit vector, at cost at most one.
A change in the initial occupation is included in that initial transition; no visit at index m is
added. For coincident visit boundaries, order the affected visits and telescope the vector changes.
The total is bounded by two for each changed interior visit and one for each changed endpoint
test. All these sides, with their original finite side intervals, are already included in (69.1). Their
complete charge is at most Bsec,end + 2Bsec,int .

Relation to the original raw target. The interval event, each collision and its unit-speed physical
time remain exact throughout. Convolution defines an analytical likelihood on those trajectories;
it is not a new physical clock or a changed return condition. The absolute estimates are uniform
even when the original roof intervals shrink arbitrarily. Dividing by their lengths, or by a small
selected-event probability, requires the corresponding additional estimate; neither is implicit here.
In particular each information restriction has its own actual denominator. A lower bound for a
larger event cannot be inherited by restriction, and a zero arithmetic event cannot be conditioned
upon. These conclusions concern νR   ∗ ; they do not automatically transfer to a stationary entrance

law with an unbounded return-roof density. The full joint spectral evaluation of (75.10), every
relevant arithmetic peak, the original endpoint-layer shortage and the four-coordinate raw local
inverse remain separate requirements. No averaged limit or finite frequency calculation is being
substituted for their proofs.

Relation to the original local problem. At fixed m the phase υm records the collision mark; it does
not create an extra coordinate beyond the original four-coordinate slice (k1 , k2 , n, t). Formula
(76.13) is evaluated on the actual physical source with the original entrance law and terminal
membership. The full chain phase is an optional observation with the exact norm stated above,
and no derivative of an arbitrary Borel trajectory selector is claimed. Such selectors are covered
by the positive likelihood estimate of Theorem 75.4 instead.
   Estimate (76.14) supplies a weak tested 1/|s| roof estimate. It is neither a strong anisotropic
transfer-operator estimate nor a decay estimate in the number of returns. In particular 1/|s|
is not integrable at infinity; absolute Fourier inversion on an expanding frequency range does
not follow from this bound alone. The arithmetic peak expansion, uniform spectral remainder,
microscopic pointwise local theorem and long-time four-coordinate inverse require their stated
additional inputs. No supremum or ordered limit in the original target is exchanged here. The
endpoint stationary-action derivative used in the proof does not replace the actual long-time
forward-orbit Jacobian in that inverse problem.

          77. Explicit reconstruction of the inherited section multipliers
   The occupation observable is the indicator of the actual section YR∗ . The historical native
section-multiplier lemma and module 84 already prove its strong multiplier property, entire
occupation phase and weak parameter continuity; modules 84–86 contain the inherited full
fixed-band spectral and arithmetic arguments. Those results are retained, with their stated
geometric and analytic hypotheses. This section supplies a fully explicit reconstruction of the
section interface and its external hypotheses. It is a proof-completeness addition, not a claim
that those multiplier or fixed-band theorems are new. No section side is rounded and no return
event is changed.
   Use the common coordinates (α, φ), with p = sin φ, and the radius-dependent arclength
s = Rα. The classical stable cones in arclength coordinates have slopes between −K and −a,
where the uniform choices
                                   a = 100/47,      K = 170/9                             (77.1)
follow from the actual curvature and flight bounds. In the common coordinates every such cone
is contained in
                     −K ≤ dφ/dα ≤ −a,          a = 45/47,      K = 799/90.                (77.2)
                         COLLISION RECORDS AND RAW LOCAL INVERSION                                241

The common cone contains the physical stable directions. The test arcs used below are tangent
to this cone, have the fixed curvature and short-length bounds, and are closed under restriction.
Invariance of the enlarged test family under every TR is a separate spectral requirement. The
sign is reversed from the unstable curves in Section 71. The change s = Rα and its inverse have
uniformly bounded derivatives on the given radius interval.
   We use precisely the stable-curve norm construction of Demers–Zhang [6, Sect. 3.3, Lemmas 5.2–
5.3]. In that construction fix common admissible exponents αDZ , βDZ , pDZ , qDZ and curve length
and curvature bounds, with 0 < qDZ < pDZ ≤ 1/3, 0 < αDZ < 1 − ς0 for the fixed summability
parameter ς0 ∈ (0, 1) of that construction, and 0 < βDZ ≤ min{αDZ , pDZ − qDZ }. The norms are
denoted ∥ · ∥B and | · |Bw on the common cylinder. The strong norm dominates the stable norm
and the weak norm tests homogeneous stable arcs against functions with C pDZ norm at most one.
Here C p has the cited little Hölder convention, the closure of smooth functions in the Hölder
norm on each test arc. The stable part has the following defining consequence: on an admissible
subarc V ,                     Z

The strong multiplier proof also applies in each radius-specific Demers–Zhang arclength space,
with common norm parameters and curve bounds. Its constants include the uniformly bounded co-
ordinate scalings. The weak difference of two moving sections is asserted on the fixed common test-
curve construction just specified; no identification of different dynamical spaces is implicit. In the
measure embedding of this construction a function h represents hν; the constant function 1 there-
fore represents ν. The coordinate expressions are dν = cos φ dα dφ/(4π) = cos φ ds dφ/(4πR).
These expressions describe the reference measure and are not a replacement of h by a density
with respect to flat area. In particular no division by cos φ is used at grazing. Lemma         R 3.4

norm constructions. They do not assert that the complete jointly twisted collision operators
already satisfy the separate hypotheses (H1)–(H5), (C1)–(C4), or the spectral conclusions of that
reference.

      79. Clearance-selected endpoint kernels and critical boundary tightness
    The endpoint layers left by Theorem 73.1 cannot be discarded by their collision-area mass.
We establish a different physical estimate: a clearance source at any flight has a small complete
endpoint-momentum kernel after propagation along its longer side. This pays the first outgoing
flight as well as the later flights. It subsequently gives a uniform tightness estimate for positive-
clearance critical sectors. The norm of that conclusion and its distinction from the original
roof-height norm are part of the statement.
    For 1 ≤ j ≤ m − 2, the selected endpoint estimate below already follows from Theorem 71.3 in
the two physical time directions. The additional first-image estimate retains a witness selected
before the first true collision and thereby completes j = 0 and j = m−1. The longer-side argument
is also present in the retained zero-clearance fan theorem 66.3; that theorem already pays its
entire zero-level stratum at the original collision normalization. The new critical conclusion here
concerns a positive clearance width, with the different norm explicitly displayed below.
    All constants and curves are those of Section 71. In particular the original radius range, the
actual first-hit map, the two impact signs and every unvisited disk are retained. Put
