            80. The exact singular part of the physical roof derivative
   The complete roof variation in Sections 74 and 76 is a finite measure. Finiteness alone does
not describe its singular part. We now identify that part on the entire physical family, including
every original section cut, unvisited boundary and critical entrance. The conclusion holds for
the actual smooth-guard and C 1 trajectory tests of (76.8); those functions are not assumed
subanalytic. The geometric decomposition is made before those weights are inserted.
   The finite physical graph and its parameterized semialgebraicity are inherited from historical
native164, not new assertions about the orbit model. Historical native40, native92 and native93
already extract and reconstruct finite-count singular germs for their specified subanalytic in-
sertions. On that older constructible scalar subclass, their finite analytic preparation together
with the retained BV bound already excludes a Cantor part; no new priority is claimed for that
consequence. Historical native153 already proves the signed projected physical boundary current
on its selected Morse charts, including the combination of coincident decision interfaces. That
signed-current principle is also inherited. The new statement here is its full physical derivative
decomposition for the current smooth observation class, with its exact physical coefficients and
the complete collision-uniform variation budget. No definability of a new observation is silently
added to the hypotheses.

80.1. Pushforward along an actual boundary side.
Lemma 80.1 (A common finite family of physical roof-side maps). Fix the true collision
count m ≥ 1. There is a finite integer Nm and, for each original radius R ∈ I, a finite set
Zm,R ⊂ [mτ− , mτ+ ], with
                                           #Zm,R ≤ Nm ,
having the following property. In the signed integration-by-parts formula for any original exact-
record roof density in Theorems 69.2 and 74.1, the regular physical boundary terms can be written
as a finite sum
                                          (tγ )∗ (bγ (r) dr).
Here r is a rational coordinate on a Gauss-direction arc, bγ ∈ L1 is the signed or complex
actual one-copy flux, and tγ is the original physical roof on that side. Each tγ is C 1 and either
constant, with value in Zm,R , or has derivative nowhere zero on its open parameter interval. The
finitely many discarded parameter points have zero flux. The positive-visited critical incoming
contributions are also supported on Zm,R .
   The same set works simultaneously for every attainable exact label, the marked phases, either
w = 1 or the original smooth guard w = W ε , and the bounded C 1 endpoint tests for which
Theorem 76.2 proves finite variation. Neither a positive incidence cutoff nor a replacement section
is used. The set is geometric: it is independent of ε, of the particular smooth function Θ, and of
these test functions or phases. No estimate uniform in m is asserted for Nm .
Proof. We spell out the physical construction because local analyticity alone would not give the
asserted finite family uniformly in R. The finite semialgebraic first-hit graph already proved in
the preserved native module 164 is the input here. We recall its defining variables, rather than
add a symbolic replacement model.
  The uniform physical horizon gives a finite set of possible next-center increments
                             A = {z ∈ Λ \ {0} : |z| ≤ τ+ + 2R+ + 1}.
For a word C0 = 0, . . . , Cm with increments in A, use real contact points Qi = Ci + Rni , unit
normals ni , unit velocities vi , and real lengths τi . The equations are
                Qi+1 = Qi + τi vi ,    vi = vi−1 − 2(vi−1 · ni )ni ,   vi−1 · ni < 0
at every visited reflection, together with the original outgoing sign at the initial collision and
τ− ≤ τi ≤ τ+ . To impose the first-hit rule, exclude an interior intersection of the actual flight
with every candidate disk preceding its designated endpoint. A disk that can meet that segment
lies within τ+ + 2R+ of its starting center. Its squared distance to the segment is determined
by the two endpoint cases and by the interior orthogonal-foot case. These are finite polynomial
inequalities after the positive projection denominator is retained. The current disk is treated
with its actual outgoing sign. No ray is restarted at a line foot.
   The same finite enlargement gives every candidate for the original least third-disk clearance.
A nearest-neighbor center other than the terminal center has distance at most 1 + R from the
initial contact, so its distance from the entire segment is at most 1 + R. The least third-disk
clearance is therefore at most 1. A minimizing center is consequently within τ+ + 2R+ + 1 of the
starting center. Square roots are encoded by their nonnegative root and squared equation. Thus
all physical incidences and original third-disk clearances are semialgebraic on this graph.
   Use finitely many rational charts for each normal circle, with one-copy ownership and the
finitely many seam sides retained until cancellation. For a fixed chart rotation the charts have
the form                                                 !

The moving center normal of each original rectangle is semialgebraic in R, because its half-angle
is the specified unique root of the original polynomial in qR . An angular side test is n · n∗ > cos h,
with its actual fixed half-width h, and its companion momentumPtest is linear. Fixed real numbers

for its true Gauss direction. The map q 7→ (F, e) has the nonzero Jacobian χ of the retained

   Now take the complete one-sided graph of these sheets in variables (R, r, t), retaining the
side identities before any observation weight is inserted. Every closure and boundary in this
construction is taken fiberwise at the fixed radius, before forming the parameterized family. For
example, membership of (r, t) in the closure of the R-fiber is expressed by
         ∀a > 0 ∃(r′ , t′ )   (R, r′ , t′ ) belongs to that sheet,   (r − r′ )2 + (t − t′ )2 < a2 .
Quantifier elimination makes this fiberwise closure semialgebraic. The fiberwise relative boundary
is obtained by the corresponding Boolean operations. Thus limits from another radius never
create physical sides at an exceptional radius. At every fixed R the regular image is open in (r, t),
so its boundary has dimension at most one. These boundaries include the original unvisited
constraints, caps used in the positive majorant, every actual section side at every collision
index, and their finite intersections. They are semialgebraic, because closure, projection and
finite Boolean operations preserve semialgebraicity. At positive visited incidences the critical
set has g = 0 and positive endpoint Hessian. Its points are isolated on each fixed-R sheet. This
is a zero-dimensional semialgebraic fiber and hence finite. Over each such critical point the
Gauss-direction closure records its actual incoming sectors at the single value t = F (q). We
keep those sectors, including unvisited-tangency corners; they are not declared null because the
physical source point is null.
   Apply C 1 cylindrical cell decomposition with R ordered before r. It is applied to the finite
geometric side graphs, their relative closures, and their projection-critical sets. A side with
nonconstant Gauss projection is then expressed on finitely many cells as t = tγ (R, r). For a
fixed radius, further refine by the semialgebraic sets where ∂r tγ is zero, positive, or negative.
On an interval in the zero set the fundamental theorem of calculus makes tγ constant. On each
remaining interval the derivative never vanishes. A side whose Gauss projection is constant has
zero dθ-flux on its regular part and does not create an omitted charge. Its intersections and the
finitely many point cells also have zero such flux. The constant values and the critical roofs form
Zm,R .
   This use of finite decomposition is precisely the finite definable-family assertion in the cell
and smooth-cell decomposition theorems, for example [10, Theorems 2.9–2.10 and 6.6–6.7].
Their hypotheses apply to the semialgebraic graphs just constructed. The finite cylindrical
                         COLLISION RECORDS AND RAW LOCAL INVERSION                                 257

decomposition has finitely many cells across the entire original radius interval, including its
exceptional parameter cells. Thus the number of its fixed-radius interval pieces, and hence the
number of their constant values and critical roofs, has a finite common upper bound Nm . These
theorems provide no upper bound independent of the formula size, which grows with m.
   The inherited physical integration-by-parts formula on a roof interval is the interior derivative
plus its signed left and right traces. For a regular side in the displayed chart, dθ = 2 dr/(1 + r2 )
up to its chosen orientation. Accordingly bγ (r) is the signed trace, including the difference
of the actual two incident record weights, times this coordinate factor. Coincident genuine
arcs have their incident values combined before assigning the flux. The physical trace and
section-charge theorems give its L1 bound; they do not require a bounded trace at each parameter
endpoint. Artificial angular charts, length cuts and homogeneity cuts cancel between their two
incident copies before this representation. At a visited grazing limit the optical trace is zero by
Lemma 67.3, including the simultaneous critical limit at its stated scope. Thus it creates no
additional side measure. The positive visited critical fan is the separately retained incoming
measure described above.
   Finally none of the smooth observation weights changes a geometric sheet or introduces a
jump side. The original W ε is continuous on each physical sheet, including where two branches
of a least clearance exchange; its interior derivative is the one already controlled in the guarded
BV proof. A bounded C 1 endpoint test similarly adds only its proved interior derivative and
multiplies existing traces. Exact labels and discrete twists are constant on the original section
chambers. They therefore change bγ and the critical sector coefficients but not the finite side
maps or their constant values. This proves the claimed common set and its scope. An arbitrary
discontinuous Borel trajectory selector does not have this conclusion.                            □

Scope. The theorem gives a common signed physical formula on the full current smooth observation
class, whose weights need not be tame, and ties all its singular derivative mass to actual constant-
roof sides and critical entrances. It does not suppress its positive critical trace, negative exit
charge or sharp integrable turning density. In particular the complete normalized local derivative
charge in (78.15) is still not proved small. The original same-roof shortage in (73.12) also retains
its exact source, comparison pool and ordered limits. All previous directed-current, paired-flux
and critical-orbit theorems remain available with their original stronger or different conclusions.
The present structural result is not presented as a rediscovery of their mechanisms.

Remark 81.2 (Coalescing roofs and the limit order). The cross term (81.11) retains coalescing
roof values. For example, the derivative δ0 − δδ of 1(0,δ) has atomic energy 2 for every δ > 0, but
finite-frequency energy 2 − 2 sin(Sδ)/(Sδ), tending to zero as δ ↓ 0 with S fixed. This analytical
check is not a substitute billiard model. A uniform variation bound alone does not justify moving
the frequency limit through a radius supremum or collision limit. Nor does the o(1/|s|) remainder
assert absolute integrability.

Relation to the unchanged raw objective. The special-BV theorem excludes a Cantor derivative
for the specified physical observations. The exact all-label spectrum identifies its atomic part
with the full signed cancellations and arithmetic labels. These results do not establish vanishing
of the remaining normalized jumps or continuous local derivative charges. Smooth narrow
spikes can have no jumps at all. The original same-roof shortage (73.12) remains the closing
condition on its existing route. The alternative sufficient bridge of Proposition 78.7 still requires
its complete normalized local derivative charge, in the original order of limits. Fixed-count
structure and the new frequency identity are not uniform dynamical estimates of that charge.
Microscopic conditioning and the four-coordinate inverse retain their actual denominator and
Jacobian hypotheses.

Lemma A.2 (Physical-time turning and the 94-flight anchor, inherited). Every actual regular
trajectory segment of physical duration H has total interior incidence cosine at least γ = 1/4480.
Every actual free flight has length at most H, and every complete 94-flight block has an interior

Proof. A collision changes the unit velocity by a vector of length 2ci . Hence for a physical

            Appendix B. An exact flux identity for unvisited near misses
   The incidence load does not see a trajectory whose original guard is witnessed only by
clearance. We introduce a counting observable on the same physical flights, not a new collision
map. Throughout this section let
                  g∗ = 1 − 2R+ = 3/50,           δ∗ = g∗ /4 = 3/200,           0 < δ ≤ δ∗ .
The symbol δ∗ here is a one-flight geometric constant, not the outer microscopic width δ(B). All
disks still have radius R.
   For a regular outgoing collision x, write its flight as q(x) + tv(x), 0 ≤ t ≤ τ (x). Let Zδ (x) be
the set of lattice centers other than the two incident centers for which
                  0<     min       |q(x) + tv(x) − z| − R < δ,       Nδ (x) = |Zδ (x)|.
                       0≤t≤τ (x)

This counts near misses, not collisions. In particular neither the collision index, the physical
roof, nor the section-visit count is incremented by Nδ . A center is counted once on a flight.

Tangencies may be assigned value zero on their collision-area null set; no assertion about a

Lemma B.1 (An interior foot and uniform endpoint separation). Every center counted by Nδ
has its perpendicular foot in the open physical flight. If tz is the time of that foot, then
                                  tz ≥ g∗ − δ,        τ − tz ≥ g∗ − δ.                              (B.1)
The candidate centers, after translating the initial incident center to zero, belong to the finite set
                                {z ∈ Λ \ {0} : |z| ≤ τ+ + 2R+ + δ∗ }.
Write N∗ for its cardinality. This constant is independent of the itinerary length and of all exact
record labels.
Proof. At either incident point, the distance to a third center is at least 1−R, since distinct lattice
centers have distance at least one. Its distance to the third disk is therefore at least 1 − 2R ≥ g∗ .
A minimum below δ ≤ g∗ /4 cannot occur at an endpoint. The nearest point on a line segment
is then its perpendicular foot, whose distance from z is at most R + δ. By the reverse triangle
inequality its distance along the line from either endpoint is at least (1 − R) − (R + δ) ≥ g∗ − δ.
Finally a foot is at distance at most R + τ+ from the initial center. Adding its distance from z
gives the finite-set bound. This proof uses the actual segment, including both of its endpoints,
rather than an infinite-line substitute for the clearance event.                                     □
   Put vϑ = (cos ϑ, sin ϑ) and vϑ⊥ = (− sin ϑ, cos ϑ). For a mark z define the signed line coordinate

oriented line with b = σ(R + u) has closest point −σ(R + u)vϑ⊥ . Follow this line backwards to its

and denote the resulting outgoing state and marked-center displacement by
                                    XR (ϑ, σ, u),       ZR (ϑ, σ, u).

closest point. The finite-horizon assumption ensures actual collisions in both directions, apart
from null singular parameters on which these maps can be defined arbitrarily. The interval from
the preceding collision to the following one remains the original physical flight.

         Appendix C. Clearance strips transverse to physical test curves
  A measure bound alone gives no short-curve control. The positive separation between an
unvisited disk and the incident disks supplies a transverse derivative which remains nonzero even
as an incident angle approaches grazing. We specify the time orientation explicitly: forward
near misses are tested on increasing-slope curves, and past-flight near misses on decreasing-slope
curves.

            Appendix H. Dependency, reference and normalization audit
   The direct clearance proofs use the original positive disk separation, the uniform finite-horizon
hypothesis, circular curvature, elastic reflection and elementary change of variables. The arbitrary-
time stable-test estimate additionally uses Input D.1. Neither uses uniform pressure, a twisted
spectral gap, or the unproved localized-shortage estimate to prove its own premise.
H.1. The precise imported curve estimate. In the inspected 10 October 2013 author version
of Demers–Zhang [6], Lemma 3.2(b), printed page 14, bounds the sum of suprema of the forward
arclength Jacobians on homogeneous inverse-image pieces, uniformly for W and for maps in the
stipulated class. The geometric-family statement is Theorem 2.7 in that version; the varying-
arclength qualification is Remark 2.9(b). The inherited module 241’s numbering must therefore
be matched to a specified version rather than silently treated as verified. Its stronger finite-testing
and pressure argument is not needed for Theorem D.2.
   For this paper the coordinates, Euclidean arclength Jacobian, short-curve curvature bound,
homogeneous partition, fixed subdivision length, and map-family constants must all agree with
Input D.1. Changing boundary perimeter with R requires the coordinate transport and its
uniform equivalence; changing the subdivision threshold changes Cg by a bounded factor. These
interfaces remain explicit retained hypotheses here, rather than a claim of an independent
specialist reconstruction.
   In the inspected 19 September 2022 author version of Baladi–Demers [7], Lemma 2.2, printed
pages 7–8, is a distortion statement across stable curves in the same homogeneous backward cell.
Its closure convention excludes true singularity curves. It is not a four-record, roof-conditioned
m−2 estimate. The present proofs make no such inference.
H.2. Checks which enter the proofs. The radius factor in (B.4) is R, not R2 or 1/R. The
two impact signs and the full direction circle give the factor 4πδ before collision normalization.
Exactly one section factor c−1∗ occurs in (E.2). The foot has physical time coordinate tz , so the
sign in (C.3) is a minus for both the boundary motion and the direction motion. Increasing-slope
curves, not forward stable curves, are used for the forward event.
   The uniform lower bounds used above are strictly positive on the whole closed radius interval:
               g∗ − δ∗ = 9/200,          κ− − (1 − R+ )−1 = 600/2491,      a0 = 9/94.
                         COLLISION RECORDS AND RAW LOCAL INVERSION                               277

The occurrence of N∗ in the curve estimate, but not in the exact flux identity, is deliberate: the
former is a one-flight union bound on a test curve, whereas the latter is a global one-copy change
of section. Empty future blocks are included by l = 0. The denominator 1 − r1−a is finite only
for a < 1; no estimate at the endpoint a = 1 is claimed.
   The source identities in the retained proof bodies are unchanged. All positive sums are
completed before essential suprema and the collision limsup. Taking B → ∞ in a stable-test
estimate would not by itself permit taking that limit in the target-roof norm. Fixed-m simulations
and symbolic identities check algebra and implementation only; they do not certify either the
inherited uniform dynamical inputs or the remaining raw pointwise theorem.
H.3. What is retained, and what has not been reconstructed. The complete active
revision-112 manuscript and its ten active core proof bodies are retained in this manuscript, and
an unmodified copy of the downloaded active packet is supplied in provenance/v112-active.
The original repository additionally contains the recursive revision-111 archive, with source
tree 790e627efe3a89a4549123d7e9acacf24089c287. That recursive archive was not exported
by the completed CI artifact available for this revision. Its identity is preserved; it has not
been represented as a locally reconstructed, independently audited set of 267 historical proofs.
The included source manifest and preservation audit distinguish byte-verified local preservation
from remote tree pinning. In particular the historical spectral, arithmetic, induced-return and
four-coordinate inverse-problem inputs are not replaced by the new clearance lemmas.

 Appendix I. Critical-roof and fold audit: normalization and ordered closure
   The new identities have different kinds of uniformity. The clearance-to-endpoint determinant
is an identity for each finite physical itinerary and every marked flight. The fold and finite-type
bounds are uniform over Borel selectors on a specified chart, with specified derivative constants.
The critical coarea error is uniform over selectors but depends on the chart’s third-derivative and
weight-modulus constants. The critical coefficient sum is over all regular physical words at fixed
collision count, relative to the retained uniform pressure input; it is unscaled. None of these
qualifiers can be replaced by another.
I.1. Two distinct uses of reversibility. At a normal endpoint, the actual reflected ray
reverses its incoming velocity. This proves the reversing-periodic-orbit assertion without adding
a reflection at an unvisited mark. In collision coordinates, time reversal also gives the derivative
identity M = JB −1 JB. The first assertion concerns actual points and their section tests; the
second concerns the tangent map on the regular domain. At an unvisited tangency, only the
one-sided reduced action coefficient is used. A smooth extension of that action does not define
the physical map through the forbidden side.
   Even at a regular reversing orbit the original section need not be reversal invariant. The
occupation identity is A2m = Am + AIm when both original endpoints are in the section, not
automatically 2n. The coefficient J describes nearby collision area pushed to the roof. It is not a
conditional law on a measure-zero periodic orbit.
I.2. The exact small-scale error and its range. The radius r0 in Theorem 17.3 is a local
endpoint-chart radius. The height increment is s = t − tx , and its allowed range is 0 < s < r02 /3.
Neither r0 nor s replaces the original microscopic observation window. In particular the explicit
error constant                          √
                                      2π 3{2Lw + Kw(0)}
has not been shown summable after multiplying the full physical source by m2 . Decreasing r0
separately for each orbit does not establish that summability. A general Borel selector retains
278                                               QIAN QI

the exact fraction aE (s); only a verified finite tangent-sector structure justifies a limiting angular
fraction.
   The local fold exponent 1/2 is produced by integrating a square-root conditional singularity
across a transverse clearance direction. A higher finite type has its stated exponent 1/ℓ and
derivative budget. Full critical roofs have a different two-dimensional local coarea law; the
fold theorem is not applied there when its clearance transversality fails. A countable disjoint
source-chart covering preserves positivity and exact multiplicity, but does not itself bound the
sum of the chart constants.
I.3. The unchanged closure statement. All original positive coefficients and the complete
nongrazing pool are still those of Section 15. The remaining statement is (15.8), with the
full physical sum first, then the exact-label and radius suprema and the original roof essential
supremum, then the collision limsup, and the outer limit last. A successful continuation must
control clearance and critical charts, positive one-sided pairing traces, the low-incidence source,
and the actual available comparison capacity in that topology. The new calculations neither
subtract these unpaid classes nor introduce a new name for the shortage.
   The accompanying programs check the signed generating derivative, stability determinant,
normalization, fold constants, selector error and actual horizontal period-two physical rays.
The latter are not asserted to lie in the large-collision central roof window. Exact rational
checks of their optical Schur complements and finite ray-derivative comparisons test independent
implementations; they are not substitutes for the written continuous proofs or the unresolved
uniform dynamical estimates.

External curve growth and physical coordinates. The inspected author version of [6] dates
from 10 October 2013. Its Lemma 3.2(b) is the homogeneous stable curve-Jacobian sum; its

   Time reversal is I(s, φ) = (s, −φ), an isometry of the original collision-coordinate arclength,
and ITR I = TR−1 on the regular set. Thus forward pieces of an unstable curve correspond to
backward pieces of its reflected stable curve, with equal arclength Jacobians. This conversion
does not reverse the original measured return record in a theorem statement; it only verifies the
curve estimate.

                 Appendix L. Current dependency and citation notes
   The preserved proof bodies retain their source-stage hypotheses and scope explanations. A later
theorem changes the current status only of the conclusion it actually proves. Thus the historical
statement that a full geometric pressure input remains to be paid is superseded by Theorem 70.4
and Corollary 70.5. This includes the original small-capacity word-supremum interface (65.19).
It does not establish abundance of the different, originally conditioned same-roof comparison pool.
The conditional consequences of Input 11.1 can now use its three native geometric conclusions
with the constants stated in Corollary 70.5.
   Theorem 67.4 supersedes the absence of a full-source unscaled roof-height bound in the earlier
weak-roof argument. Its interior variation, all-offset regular unvisited boundaries, complete
critical sectors, cap endpoints and inherited zero visited-grazing trace are explicitly accounted for.
The proof does not assert zero trace for a different pairing construction or a bound for its singular
multiplier. Theorem 68.6 pays every actual finite section side in the specified roof variation
topology. Theorem 69.2 restores the exact occupation, lattice labels, initial conditioning and
terminal test. Its joint marked Fourier estimate is (69.8); it is uniform in the mark frequencies
but has only an |s|−1 roof bound.
   Theorems 64.1, 65.3 and 66.3 are inherited from the complete immediate predecessor. They
respectively give the all-offset regular marked-boundary budget, all-class physical capacity
moment, and leading positive-visited incoming critical-fan payment. Their proof bodies and
provenance are unchanged. The new endpoint argument does not relabel these results as new
contributions, or claim a uniform local Taylor remainder solely from a leading coefficient.
   The new Theorem 71.1 retains selected source length in the complete physical branch-supremum
sum. Its own enlarged curve class, cutoff and constants are fixed in (71.1)–(71.2). Theorem 72.4
combines this transport with all actual outgoing boundary charges, the exact cap Jacobian
cancellation and the full localized singular multiplier. Non-grazing critical fan values are retained
as incoming traces. Theorem 73.1 pays all sufficiently deep clearance witnesses at the original m2
roof-height scale. This supersedes the earlier absence of a normalized payment for that precise
subsource; it does not pay the shallow source. Theorem 73.2 proves that the original shortage is
equivalent to (73.12), with exactly the same full comparison pool and order of limits.

      Appendix M. Dependency scope of the physical jump-spectrum continuation
   The preceding appendix is retained byte for byte from the immediate complete predecessor.
Its source-stage descriptions of new results refer to that historical continuation. The current
priority, source identity and proof status are those recorded in the introduction and the present
appendix.
The present complete derivative and jump-spectrum interface. Theorems 80.3 and 81.1
identify the exact singular derivative and its marked Fourier energy for the full current smooth
observation class. The finite physical graph is inherited from native 164, the scalar tame-germ
consequences from native 40, 92 and 93, and the signed-current principle from native 153. The
new proofs require the complete signed source and norm budget of native 323, 324, 330 and 332,
whose continuous dynamical inputs remain author proofs with their stated hypotheses, rather
than independently certified facts. The finite side decomposition uses fixed-radius closures and
the definable-family cell theorems [10, Theorems 2.9–2.10 and 6.6–6.7]. It is applied to geometry,
not to arbitrary C 1 weights.
   The equality of variation masses in (80.5) concerns the derivative after signed cancellations. It
does not identify a positive majorant with that signed measure. In particular a critical incoming
coefficient can meet a negative constant-roof side coefficient. All same-label roof coincidences are
combined before squaring in (81.4). The fixed-count frequency limit is never exchanged with the
original collision limsup or a radius supremum.
   The normalized central jump bound is necessary for the raw target. Its converse is not asserted:
a continuous narrow peak has zero jump energy. The original complete local derivative charge of
native 334 still includes both the integrable derivative and all its actual atoms. The old zero-
clearance payment of native 322 transfers to the new energy through (81.15); the positive-width
and other remaining charges are not thereby paid. No claim of full raw or inverse closure is
added by the present two modules.
